findings.suggested_fix: Split REQ-13 into: (a) opened from the tile, the list applies no status filter (A-02); (b) a status filter chosen afterwards combines with the period filter (ticket L24).
findings.text: REQ-13 is compound: it states the list opens with no status filter from the tile, and separately that a status filter chosen later combines with the period. A-02 only decides the first; the second is a separate testable behaviour.

rubric_items.reason: All nine acceptance criteria map to REQ-1..REQ-14; AC6 is now split into REQ-6, REQ-7, REQ-13, REQ-14; API filter design is out of scope with a reason.
F-1 fixed: REQ-7 covers search only. REQ-13 still bundles two behaviours: no status filter on opening from the tile, and a later status filter combining with the period.
Every REQ cites a ticket line; REQ-2 and REQ-13 cite the user's answers A-01 and A-02; no assumed or invented values.
The AC3/AC5 vs AC6 status-filter tension was asked as Q-02, answered in A-02, and recorded as a mismatch citing ticket L24.
Q-01 and Q-02 were precise, with a proposed default and a real alternative; both answered; no needless open questions.
Plain words; Period, Tile, Inactive used consistently; the undefined glossary term registered is noted in Out of scope.
